source_text: Ἰουδαῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ νῦν διδάσκουσι τὸν ἀνωνόμαστον θεὸν λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωυσεῖ. Ὁθεν τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προμεμηνυμένου προφήτου ἐλέγχον αὐτούς, ὡς προεγράψαμεν, εἶπεν· „Ἔγνω βοῦς τὸν κτησάμενον καὶ ὄνος τὴν φάτνην τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ Ἰησοῦς δὲ ὁ Χριστός, ότι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν Ἰουδαῖοι, τί πατὴρ καὶ τί υἱός, ὁμοίως ἐλέγχων αὐτοὺς καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἀποκαλύψῃ ὁ υἱός“. Ὁ λόγος δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ ἄγγελος δὲ καλεῖται καὶ ἀπόστολος· αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀπαγγέλλει, ὅσα δεῖ γνωσθῆναι, καὶ ἀποστέλλεται μηνύσων, ὅσα ἀγγέλλεται, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἱ κύριος ἡμῶν εἶπεν· „Ὁ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων ἀκούει τοῦ ἀποστείλαντός με“. Καὶ ἐκ τῶν τοῦ Μωϋσέως δὲ συγγραμμάτων φανερὸν τοῦτο γενήσεται. Λέλεκται δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς οὕτως· „Καὶ ἐλάλησε Μωϋσεῖ ἄγγελος θεοῦ ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς ἐκ τῆς βάτου καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, θεὸς Ἀβραάμ, θεὸς Ἰσαάκ, θεὸς Ἰακώβ, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου. Κάτελθε εἰς Αἰγυπτον καὶ ἐξάγαγε τὸν λαόν μου“. Τὰ δ᾿ ἑπόμενα ἐξ ἐκείνων βουλόμενοι μαθεῖν δύνασθε· οὐ γὰρ δυνατὸν ἐν τούτοις ἀναγράψαι πάντα. Ἀλλ᾿ εἰς ἀπόδειξιν γεγόνασιν οἵδε οἱ λόγοι, ότι υἱὸς θεοῦ καὶ ἀπόστολος ᾿Ιησοῦς ὁ Χριστός ἐστι, πρότερον λόγος ὤν, καὶ ἐν ἰδέᾳ πυρὶ ς ποτὲ φανείς, ποτὲ δὲ καὶ ἐν εἰκόνι ἀσωμάτῳ· νῦν δὲ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου γένους ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος ὑπέμεινε καὶ παθεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸν ἐνήργησαν οἱ δαίμονες διατεθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνοήτων Ἰουδαίων. Οἵτινες ἔχοντες ῥητῶς εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς Μωϋσέως συντάγμασι· „Καὶ ἐλάλησεν ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ Μωϋσεῖ ἐν πυρὶ φλογὸς ἐν βάτῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ἱ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ“, τὸν τῶν όλων πατέρα καὶ δημιουργὸν τὸν ταῦτα εἰπόντα λέγουσιν εἶναι. Ὅθεν καὶ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα ἐλέγχον αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· „Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω, καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ὡς ἐδηλώσαμεν, παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἂν εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μἰ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἱ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψῃ“. Ἰουδαῖοι οὖν ἡγησάμενοι ἀεὶ τὸν πατέρα τᾶν ὅλων λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωϋσεῖ, τοῦ λαλήσαντος αὐτῷ ὄντος υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἀπόστολος κέκληται, δικαίως ἐλέγχονται καὶ διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς οὔτε τὸν πατέρα οὔτε τὸν υἱὸν ἔγνωσαν. Οἱ γὰρ τὸν υἱὸν πατέρα φάσκοντες εἶναι ἐλέγχονται μήτε τὸν πατέρα ἐπιστάμενοι, μηθ᾿ ότι ἐστὶν υἱὸς τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων γινώσκοντες· ὃς λόγος καὶ πρωτότοκος ὢν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ θεὶς ὑπάρχει. Καὶ πρότερον διὰ τῆς τοῦ πυρὸς μορφῆς καὶ εἰκόνος ἀσωμάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἑτέροις προφήταις ἐφάνη· νῦν δ᾿ ἐν χρόνοις τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀρχῆς, ὡς προείπομεν, διὰ παρθένου ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς βουλὴν ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας τῶν πιστευόντων αὐτῷ καὶ ἐξουθενηθῆναι καὶ παθεῖν ὑπέμενεν, ἵνα ἀποθανὼν καὶ ἀναστὰς νικήσῃ τὸν θάνατον. Τὶ δὲ εἰρημένον ἐκ βάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ· „Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακὼβ καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου“, σημαντικὸν τοῦ καὶ ἀποθανόντας ἐκείνους μένειν καὶ εἶναι αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀνθρώπους· καὶ γὰρ πρῶτοι τῶν πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐκεῖνοι περὶ θεοῦ ζήτησιν ἠσχολήθησαν, Ἀβραὰμ μὲν πατὴρ ὢν τοῦ Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ τοῦ Ἰακώβ, ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἀνέγραψε.
pass_a_gloss: The Jews, however, all teach that the unnamed God spoke to Moses. Therefore, the prophetic Spirit, through Isaiah the aforementioned prophet, rebuked them, as we have written, saying: 'The ox knows the one who acquired it, and the donkey the manger of its Lord, but Israel does not know me, and the people do not understand me.' And Jesus the Christ, because the Jews did not know what Father and what Son are, similarly rebuked them, saying: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son reveals Him.' The Word of God is the Son of God, as we have previously said. And He is also called an angel and an apostle, for He announces what must be known and is sent to proclaim what He announces, just as the Lord Himself said: 'The one who hears me hears the one who sent me.' This will become clear from the writings of Moses. For it is written in them: 'And the angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers. Go down to Egypt and lead out my people.' Those who wish to learn the rest can do so from those writings, for it is not possible to write everything here. But these words have come as a proof that Jesus the Christ is the Son of God and an apostle, who was previously the Word and appeared at times in the form of fire and at times in an incorporeal image; now, however, He has become a man through the will of God for the sake of the human race and endured suffering, which the demons, through the senseless Jews, inflicted upon Him. The Jews, who have it explicitly stated in the writings of Moses: 'And the angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob,' say that the Father of all, the Creator, who said these things, is the one who spoke. Therefore, the prophetic Spirit, rebuking them, said: 'But Israel does not know me, and the people do not understand me.' And again, Jesus, as we have shown, would say to them: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son reveals Him.' The Jews, then, having always thought that the Father of all spoke to Moses, whereas it was the Son of God who spoke to him, who is also called an angel and an apostle, are justly rebuked both through the prophetic Spirit and through Christ Himself, since they did not know either the Father or the Son. For those who claim that the Son is the Father are rebuked for not knowing the Father and for not understanding that there is a Son of the Father of all, who is the Word and the firstborn of God and exists as God. And previously, through the form of fire and an incorporeal image, He appeared to Moses and the other prophets; now, however, in the time of your reign, as we have previously said, He became a man through a virgin, according to the will of the Father, for the salvation of those who believe in Him, and endured to be despised and to suffer, so that having died and risen, He might conquer death. What was said to Moses from the bush: 'I am the one who is, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob and the God of your fathers,' is significant, because even though they died, they remain and are people of Christ; for they were the first of all people to be concerned with the search for God, Abraham being the father of Isaac, and Isaac the father of Jacob, as Moses also wrote.

choices.why: The Greek text uses the word ἀνωνόμαστος to describe God, indicating that God's name is not explicitly stated.
The Greek text uses the phrase προφητικὸν πνεῦμα to refer to the Spirit that speaks through the prophets.
The Greek text uses the word ἄγγελος to describe Jesus, indicating that He is a messenger of God.

pass_b_english: The Jews still all teach that the unnamed God spoke to Moses. Therefore, the prophetic Spirit, through the prophet Isaiah mentioned above, rebuked them — as we have written — saying: "The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel does not know me, and my people do not understand me" (Isaiah 1:3). Jesus the Christ likewise rebuked them because the Jews did not know what Father and what Son are, saying: "No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him" (Matthew 11:27). The Word of God is the Son of God, as we previously said. He is also called an angel and an apostle, for he announces what must be known and is sent to proclaim what he announces, just as the Lord himself said: "Whoever hears me hears the one who sent me" (Matthew 10:40). This will become clear from the writings of Moses, for it is written there: "And an angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers. Go down to Egypt and lead out my people" (Exodus 3:2, 6, 10). Those who wish to learn the rest can do so from those writings, for it is not possible to write everything here.

But these words have come as proof that Jesus the Christ is the Son of God and an apostle. He was previously the Word and appeared at times in the form of fire and at times in an incorporeal image; now, however, through the will of God, he became a man for the sake of the human race, endured suffering, and submitted to the treatment that the demons, through the senseless Jews, inflicted upon him. The Jews, who have it explicitly stated in the writings of Moses: "And an angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob" (Exodus 3:2, 6), claim that the Father of all, the Creator who said these things, is the one who spoke. Therefore the prophetic Spirit, rebuking them, said: "But Israel does not know me, and the people do not understand me" (Isaiah 1:3). And again Jesus, as we have shown, would say to them: "No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son reveals him" (Matthew 11:27). The Jews, then, having always thought that the Father of all spoke to Moses, whereas it was the Son of God who spoke to him — who is also called an angel and an apostle — are justly rebuked both through the prophetic Spirit and through Christ himself, since they knew neither the Father nor the Son.

For those who claim that the Son is the Father are rebuked for not knowing the Father and for not understanding that there is a Son of the Father of all, who is the Word, the firstborn of God, and exists as God. And previously, through the form of fire and an incorporeal image, he appeared to Moses and the other prophets; now, however, in the time of your reign, as we previously said, he became a man through a virgin according to the will of the Father for the salvation of those who believe in him. He endured to be despised and to suffer, so that by dying and rising he might conquer death. What was said to Moses from the bush — "I am the one who is, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob and the God of your fathers" (Exodus 3:6) — is significant because even though they died, those patriarchs remain and are people of Christ; for they were the first of all people to be concerned with the search for God, Abraham being the father of Isaac and Isaac the father of Jacob, as Moses also wrote.
